sites.name: Personal Writing
sites.summary: A warm personal publication that pairs an editorial front door with an index and a lightweight private studio.
sites.designSummary: The system feels like a small periodical rather than a blog template. Newsreader carries the voice, DM Sans keeps navigation direct, and DM Mono handles coordinates, issue numbers, and tool states. Fine rules and a muted paper palette make the interface feel collected without making it precious.
sites.layout: A wide editorial header leads into large two-column feature fields; archive and reading pages use narrow indexes beside generous text columns.
sites.interactions: Slow reading progress, restrained hover color, small directional shifts, and a mobile menu that preserves the publication hierarchy.
sites.pattern: Editorial front door with numbered archive views
sites.caution: Restrained navigation should still expose search, current state, and studio boundaries.

sites.name: Signal Notes
sites.summary: A dark startup research archive combining a concise company table with deeper profile notes, product diagrams, and competitive context.
sites.designSummary: Signal Notes uses an instrument-panel vocabulary without becoming a dashboard. A monochrome shell, technical labels, and measured orange signals leave room for product explanations and long research notes. Logos behave as data marks rather than decorative tiles.
sites.layout: A table-first overview branches into vertically organized company profiles with wide narrative and diagram modules.
sites.interactions: Center-out row reveals, slow detection pulses, hash routes, and progressive disclosure between brief and full profile notes.
sites.pattern: Persistent section rail plus progressive disclosure
sites.caution: Technical diagrams and motion can overpower reading unless their job stays explicit.

sites.name: MotionDeck Studio
sites.summary: A light technical workspace for browsing, creating, and connecting visual assets across distinct production modes.
sites.designSummary: MotionDeck behaves like a creative operating system. Its neutral workspace lets vivid previews carry the personality while small labels, strong grouping, and compact controls keep production state legible.
sites.layout: Persistent library rail, central canvas, and contextual settings form a stable three-column production shell.
sites.interactions: Mode changes preserve workspace context; hover and selected states rely on borders, small shadows, and controlled color rather than motion-heavy transitions.
sites.pattern: Dense library navigation with task-oriented modes
sites.caution: High control counts need strong grouping, reliable defaults, and clear empty states.

sites.name: Fleeting
sites.summary: A dark game-development workbook that makes systems, playtests, and roadmap state visible beside the playable idea.
sites.designSummary: Fleeting turns documentation into part of the game world. Bright system colors mark different mechanics against a deep background, while numbered routes and compact ledgers make a complicated prototype feel inspectable.
sites.layout: A chaptered workbook alternates wide concept frames with dense system tables and playable modules.
sites.interactions: Hover traces and subtle glow reinforce active systems; navigation behaves like a technical manual rather than marketing pages.
sites.pattern: Numbered navigation and living design documentation
sites.caution: Workbook depth can make the primary playable action ambiguous.

sites.name: Kaggriculture Fieldbook
sites.summary: A strategy fieldbook for game mechanics, agents, experiments, and findings, presented as a living agricultural notebook.
sites.designSummary: The Fieldbook uses the language of plots, seasons, and experiments to organize systems thinking. Earth tones give the technical workbook a specific world, while status chips and ruled tables make simulation details easy to scan.
sites.layout: A persistent workbook index opens into full-width strategy tables, experiment summaries, and agent notes.
sites.interactions: State changes are conveyed through chips and selection rules; motion is kept secondary to legibility.
sites.caution: Monospace at reading scale can flatten hierarchy and exhaust longer notes.

sites.name: SoundDeck
sites.summary: A light audio workbench that organizes generation, takes, projects, and connectors around a single production surface.
sites.designSummary: SoundDeck treats audio as a visual material. Waveforms and take states carry the color while the surrounding shell remains quiet, reducing the cognitive load of moving between generation, review, and assembly.
sites.layout: An asset palette and project rail frame a central production timeline with contextual actions nearby.
sites.interactions: Playback state, selection, and generation progress use clear visual feedback and minimal layout movement.
sites.pattern: Asset palette paired with a production workspace
sites.caution: Large tool surfaces need clear empty, loading, and destructive-action states.

sites.name: Cost Basis
sites.summary: A finance notebook with generous editorial scale, warm paper, and structured archive views for personal analysis.
sites.designSummary: Cost Basis makes finance feel considered rather than terminal-like. Large serif headings carry the argument, while tabular figures, thin rules, and small mono metadata preserve the precision expected of financial notes.
sites.layout: Publication-scale essays sit beside compact metadata and structured archive tables.
sites.interactions: Reading progress and restrained row states support navigation without introducing dashboard behavior.
sites.pattern: Publication shell around a personal research system
sites.caution: Writing tools and private data should remain visually and technically separate from public reading.

sites.name: Pokémon Rogue Dungeons
sites.summary: A terrain-colored prototype that links a runnable expedition with its own design documentation.
sites.designSummary: The project uses terrain, inventory, and encounter language as both interface and documentation. Playful pixel forms create identity, while a cleaner supporting typeface keeps system notes legible outside the play surface.
sites.layout: A playable expedition is embedded inside a chaptered design workbook with rules and encounter notes.
sites.interactions: Direct tile and card feedback is immediate; documentation views use calmer, conventional controls.
sites.pattern: Playable object embedded inside its own design workbook
sites.caution: Novel visual language still needs conventional focus, hover, and completion feedback.

sites.name: Margins and Weather
sites.summary: An editorial deployment built from the same publication architecture as Personal Writing, with a quieter atmospheric identity.
sites.designSummary: This publication tests how far a stable editorial system can travel through token changes alone. Clouded neutrals and weather-map blue shift the mood while the issue structure, reading measures, and navigation stay familiar.
sites.layout: A reusable publication shell with editorial home, index, article, about, and studio views.
sites.interactions: Subtle progress and hover cues maintain the calm reading system inherited from the base publication.
sites.pattern: Reusable publication starter with swappable identity
sites.caution: A shared template needs meaningful token and content variation to avoid clone-like results.

sites.name: Worth More?
sites.summary: A valuation game that pairs a simple decision loop with deeper insight and data-studio views.
sites.designSummary: Worth More? turns comparative valuation into a repeatable game. Big numeric prompts and binary decisions create an immediate loop; deeper data views reuse the same typographic and color logic so analysis feels like a continuation rather than a separate product.
sites.layout: A focused single-question play surface opens into history, insight, and data-studio views.
sites.interactions: Fast choice feedback, animated value reveals, and streak state make the loop playful without obscuring the numbers.
sites.pattern: Game mechanic as an entry point to structured data
sites.caution: Analytical depth should not interrupt the speed and clarity of the core play loop.

sites.name: Good Places, Together
sites.summary: A warm map-first restaurant guide built around place memory and shared recommendations rather than rankings.
sites.designSummary: The guide treats a recommendation as a memory attached to a place. Warm cartographic colors, handwritten-feeling editorial moments, and restrained controls keep the map personal rather than transactional.
sites.layout: A map and editorial place cards share the viewport, with filters and details appearing only when needed.
sites.interactions: Pins, cards, and list selection stay synchronized; mobile shifts from split view to a clear map-or-list mode.
sites.pattern: Spatial browsing with an editorial point of view
sites.caution: Map controls and narrative cards compete for scarce attention on small screens.
